## Control and timing

#### ★☆☆ Optimum settings for automatic controllers

Ziegler & Nichols · 1942 · *Transactions of the ASME* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Optimum%20settings%20for%20automatic%20controllers%22)

- **Why:** The first PID tuning rules (1942), still quoted everywhere.
- **Read:** The two tuning methods.

#### ★★☆ Advanced PID Control

Åström & Hägglund · 2006 · *ISA* · book · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Advanced%20PID%20Control%22)

- **Why:** Everything the tuning rules leave out: windup, filtering, set-point weighting.
- **Read:** The chapters on PID structure and tuning.

#### ★★★ Scheduling algorithms for multiprogramming in a hard-real-time environment

Liu & Layland · 1973 · *Journal of the ACM* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Scheduling%20algorithms%20for%20multiprogramming%20in%20a%20hard-real-time%20environment%22)

- **Why:** Rate-monotonic scheduling: how to assign RTOS priorities with guarantees.
- **Read:** The utilization bound.

#### ★★★ Priority inheritance protocols: An approach to real-time synchronization

Sha, Rajkumar & Lehoczky · 1990 · *IEEE Transactions on Computers* · paper · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22Priority%20inheritance%20protocols%3A%20An%20approach%20to%20real-time%20synchronization%22)

- **Why:** Priority inheritance, which your RTOS mutexes must enable.
- **Read:** §1–3.

#### ★★☆ High-Speed Digital Design: A Handbook of Black Magic

Johnson & Graham · 1993 · *Prentice Hall* · book · [Scholar ↗](https://scholar.google.com/scholar?q=%22High-Speed%20Digital%20Design%3A%20A%20Handbook%20of%20Black%20Magic%22)
